basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 5.' and it opens '(Vers. 5 et 6.) Simeon et Levi fratres consummaverunt iniquitatem adinventionis suae: in'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 5 et 6.) Simeon et Levi fratres consummaverunt iniquitatem adinventionis suae: in consilium eorum non veniat anima mea: et in congregatione eorum non aemuletur jecur meum, quia in furore suo interfecerunt homines, et in desiderio suo subnervaverunt taurum. Necessitate compellimur juxta propositum operis longius ea repetere, quae ab Hebraica veritate discordant. Legitur enim ibi: Simeon et Levi fratres, vasa iniquitatis arma eorum. In arcanum eorum, ne intret anima mea, et in conventu eorum ne desoletur gloria mea, quia in furore suo interfecerunt virum, et in libidine sua suffoderunt murum (Gen. XXXIV). Significat autem non sui consilii fuisse, quod Sichem et Emor foederatos viros interfecerint, contraque jus pacis et amicitiarum sanguinem fuderint innocentem, et quasi quodam furore, sic crudelitate rapti, muros hospitae urbis everterint.
